Paul Delos Santos is a reporter based in Las Vegas. He covers the Vegas Golden Knights forNHL.comand also covers esports and general Las Vegas sports for The Sporting Tribune. He’s a gamer who never has time to play them, so he naturally opted to write and talk about them instead.

Olivia Richman is a seasoned esports journalist who has worked with Inven Global, Esports Illustrated, Esports.gg, and more. As an editor and writer at Esports Insider, she loves telling unique esports stories, especially within the FGC. When not working and gaming, Olivia loves collecting Kirby plush, eating sushi, and driving her cars at the track.

FlyQuest junglerJohnson “Griffynn” Lemoved to Korea at 16 years old to try and climb up the region’s brutalLeague of Legendsplayer development system.

It was uncomfortable, especially since – by his estimation – he probably could have been in the LCS by then. But the lure of playing in the hotbed of the game in one of the most prestigious academies in the world (T1 – home of Faker) as one of the first foreigners in the academy was too much to pass up.

“It just seemed like at the time … it was a no-brainer,” he said to Esports Insider.

But while he valued his time in Korea, it wasn’t until he went to Brazil that he saw his gameplay take major steps forward.
